culture-cycles.public_holidays: Anguilla public holidays still to come in 2026: Friday 18 December (National Heroes and Heroines Day); Friday 25 December (Christmas Day); Monday 28 December (Boxing Day). Earlier in 2026: Monday 2 March (James Ronald Webster Day); Monday 1 June (Anguilla Day); Monday 22 June (King's Birthday celebration); Monday 3, Thursday 6 and Friday 7 August (August Monday, August Thursday, Constitution Day). The Government portal lists an addendum to public holidays for 2027; its dates were not read.

facts.label: E-residency
facts.text: No official e-residency programme for foreigners (a government digital identity that is not a residence permit) was found in this pass. If the country offers official digital ID or electronic signatures for residents or citizens, that is noted only where an official agency is linked.

facts.label: Official digital or government services
facts.text: Start with Government of Anguilla for official digital-identity, electronic-signature or e-government services and renewals.

digital-residency.notes: Short visitor visas and entry formalities are covered under Entry and Visa preparation, not this pattern.

physical-residency.summary: Official temporary and permanent residency routes in Anguilla, with presence and costs where published.

facts.label: Official residence authority
facts.text: Temporary and permanent residence routes for foreigners are administered by Immigration Department, Government of Anguilla. Read the current official route names, minimum presence and fees on that site.

facts.label: Scope
facts.text: This pattern covers official temporary and permanent residency, including published minimum presence and costs where known. It does not cover short visitor visas, which sit under Entry and Visa preparation.

sources.title: Immigration Department, Government of Anguilla
sources.supports: official residence and immigration authority

citizenship.summary: Official naturalisation, descent and dual-citizenship rules in Anguilla, for an Australian passport holder.

facts.label: Dual citizenship (destination rule)
facts.text: Whether the destination allows dual citizenship should be confirmed on the official nationality pages. Do not assume that a residence permit leads to citizenship, or that Australia's rule applies there.

facts.label: Citizenship by descent
facts.text: Many countries have a descent route with official documentary conditions. Confirm eligibility on the official nationality pages before planning around it.

facts.label: Official authority
facts.text: Start with Immigration Department, Government of Anguilla for official naturalisation, descent and dual-citizenship rules.

citizenship.notes: Australian law also matters: Australia allows its citizens to hold another citizenship. That does not change the destination country's own dual-citizenship rules.

sources.title: Immigration Department, Government of Anguilla
sources.supports: official citizenship or nationality authority

intellectual-property.summary: Official patents, trademarks, licensing and IP ownership in Anguilla.

facts.label: Official IP office
facts.text: Anguilla is a UK overseas territory and is not listed as its own WIPO member in the official IP-office directory. Official UK IP law and the UK IPO are the usual starting point, together with official Anguilla government pages.

facts.label: Official IP office
facts.text: Patents, trademarks and related official registers start with Intellectual Property Office (United Kingdom).

facts.label: Ownership, licensing and filing
facts.text: Foreign ownership of IP, official licensing formalities, and whether the system is first-to-file, should be confirmed on the official IP office pages (and, where listed, on WIPO Lex). This pass records the official office rather than a full statute summary.
